blocks.prompt: 2 Prove that \(\overline{z} = z\) iff \(z\) is real.
blocks.explanation: Yeh proof ka sawal hai, aur is mein lafz "iff" bohat aham hai. "iff" ka matlab hai "if and only if" (agar aur sirf agar), yani humein do taraf saabit karna hai, jaise aik pul jo dono taraf se guzarne ke qabil ho: (a) agar \(\overline{z} = z\) ho to \(z\) real hai; (b) agar \(z\) real ho to \(\overline{z} = z\). Sirf aik taraf saabit karna adhoora jawab hai. Tool hum yeh use karenge: \(z = a + ib\) likhein; conjugate (ulta sign wala saathi) \(\overline{z} = a - ib\) hai; aur \(z\) real tab hota hai jab \(b = 0\) ho.
steps:
Step 1: \(z\) aur \(\overline{z}\) ko letters mein likhein
\[z = a + ib, \; a, b \in \mathbb{R}\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: Har complex number ko is shakal mein likha ja sakta hai, is liye jo baat \(a\) aur \(b\) ke liye saabit hogi woh har complex number ke liye sach hogi. Conjugate sirf imaginary part ka sign badalta hai; real part waisa hi rehta hai, jaise real axis mein aaine ka aks.

Step 2 (hissa a): Farz karein \(\overline{z} = z\)
\[a - ib = a + ib\]
\[-ib - ib = 0\]
\[-2ib = 0\]
\[b = 0\]
Kyun: Dono taraf se \(a + ib\) minus kiya: \(a\) cancel ho gaya aur \(-ib - ib = -2ib\) bacha. \(-2i\) zero nahin hai, is liye dono taraf ko \(-2i\) se divide kar sakte hain, aur \(b = 0\) mil jata hai.

Step 3: Natija: \(z\) real hai
\[z = a + i(0) = a\]
Kyun: \(b = 0\) ka matlab imaginary part khatam. Ab \(z\) sirf real number \(a\) reh gaya. Pehli taraf saabit ho gayi.

Step 4 (hissa b): Farz karein \(z\) real hai
\[z = a + i(0) = a\]
\[\overline{z} = a - i(0) = a\]
\[\overline{z} = z\]
Kyun: Real number mein \(b = 0\) hota hai, aur 0 ka sign badalne se 0 hi rehta hai (\(-0 = 0\)). Is liye conjugate lene se kuch nahin badla. Doosri taraf bhi saabit.
Dhyan dein: Exam mein dono hisson ko (a) aur (b) ke label ke saath likhein, taake examiner ko saaf nazar aaye ke "iff" ki dono directions saabit ki gayi hain.

Step 5: Dono hisse jor dein
Hissa (a) ne saabit kiya "agar \(\overline{z} = z\) to \(z\) real", aur hissa (b) ne ulti taraf "agar \(z\) real to \(\overline{z} = z\)". Dono mil kar "iff" wala poora statement saabit karte hain.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal: \(z = 5\) ho to \(\overline{z} = 5\), barabar. Lekin \(z = 5 + 2i\) ho to \(\overline{z} = 5 - 2i\), jo \(z\) ke barabar nahin, kyun ke yahan \(b \ne 0\). Yani jab tak imaginary part hai, number apne aaine ke aks jaisa nahin hota.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\overline{z} = z\) tab aur sirf tab jab \(z\) real ho (yani real numbers hi woh numbers hain jo real axis ke aaine mein apni jagah par rehte hain).
